chunks: Design a multiplexer (mux). The question: Design a mux.
A multiplexer, or mux, is a digital switch that passes exactly one of several inputs to a single output. A control input, called the select, chooses which one.
It is the hardware version of an if statement. Chips use muxes everywhere.
Think of a railway junction. Several tracks arrive, one track leaves, and a lever decides which arriving track is connected to the outgoing one.
Flip the lever, and a different track feeds the output.
One caution: if the lever moves at the wrong instant, the output can flicker, which matters only if it drives a clock (the beat that paces a chip).
The inverter makes the complement of S. The top AND passes A only when S = 0, the bottom AND passes B only when S = 1, and the OR merges the two.
Exactly one AND can be active, so the OR just forwards it.
Select line: the control input that chooses which data input reaches the output. One-hot: a signal with exactly one bit set. Gates: tiny logic circuits.
An inverter flips 0 and 1, AND gives 1 only if all inputs are 1, and OR gives 1 if any input is 1.
Inferred latch: an unwanted memory element created when code forgets to set the output on some path. Glitch: a very short wrong pulse on a signal that should stay steady.
Parameter: a setting in RTL (hardware description) code, such as data width, so one block serves many uses.
A 2:1 mux has data inputs A and B and a select S. The output is Y equals S A plus S B , read as "(not S) AND A, OR S AND B", so S = 0 passes A and S = 1 passes B.
If A = 1 and B = 0, then Y = 1 when S = 0, and Y = 0 when S = 1. In gates, that is one inverter, two ANDs and an OR. A 4:1 mux is three 2:1 muxes.
In general an N:1 mux needs N-1 of them in log 2 N levels. That is the whole idea.
"A mux picks one of several inputs based on a select. For a 2:1 it's Y equals not-S times A plus S times B, one inverter, two ANDs, an OR.
In RTL I'd write a parameterized assign y = sel ? b : a , or an indexed array for N inputs with no latch.
Scaling to N inputs gives a tree of N minus one 2:1 muxes, log2 N deep, or a flat AND-OR if the select is one-hot.
I'd also mention that an AND-OR mux can glitch when both inputs are 1 and the select flips, which matters if the output is a clock."
Quick check. Which Boolean expression describes a 2:1 mux with select S, data inputs A (S = 0) and B (S = 1)?
